meta.title: Aunt Sue Comes to Our House

paragraphs: Aunt Sue comes to our house on Saturday. She takes a bus from the city, and she does not know our street. I write a message for her. Get off the bus at the bus stop near the school. Walk along the big road for five minutes. Go straight, and do not turn. The road is busy and dangerous, so look left and right. Cross the road at the crossing next to the fruit shop. You can buy mangoes there. I think Mom likes mangoes.

Turn left at the corner of the fruit shop. Our street is next to the park. Walk by the park and look for a white house. The house has a red gate. A sign on the gate says "Please close the gate." You may be surprised and ask, "What does it mean?" It means that Pip is in the garden. He is small, but he runs very quickly. Pip waits behind the gate, and he says, "Woof!"

Now you are at our house. Take off your shoes and put them next to the door. Mom is in the kitchen, and Dad is on the sofa. Tom is in his room, and Pip runs in and goes under the table. Your room is upstairs. Your room is next to Tom's room. Your bed is under the window. Is it difficult? I do not think so! Aunt Sue, we are happy to see you.
text.summary: Lily writes the way from the bus stop to her house for Aunt Sue. She also tells her where things are inside the house.
